messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Re: Analysing 50+ days of accelerometry
messages.body_plain:
Hi Justin,

There is no day limit to part 4 or 5, only in part 2 there is an arbitrary limit of 26 weeks.
The nnpp = 40 which Vahan found in the code does not apply here. It relates to argument do.visual in function g.part4. This creates a pdf with 40 nights per page from an entire study. If there are more nights it will simply keep creating new pages in the pdf until all nights are visualised.

Do you get 38 days for both the MM and WW reports in part5?
I think that changing excludefirstlast = TRUE to excludefirstlast = FALSE will give you the 40 days of data.

Note that with excludefirstlast = TRUE you tell GGIR to ignore the first and last night, which then influences the number of days/nights part5 can work with. As a result, it is not surprising to have 2 nights/days less in part 5 compared with part 2 for example.

Best, Vincent

On Wed, 24 Oct 2018 at 01:28, John <karh...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi all,
>
> I am currently analysing 24-h dataset for my research project and I wonder if anyone could share your thoughts of which output variables from Part 5 SUMMARY file should be included to get a 24h distribution among all behaviours (sleep, sedentary behaviour and PA)?
> Below are those variables which I think representative of the 24-hr analysis:
>

Response: Go to the MM report (Midnight to minight) as created by part5. There you will notice that only a specific consecutive series of variables will always add up to exactly 24 hours (1440 minutes), typically starting with column "dur_nightsleep_min". The number of columns you need to arrive at a sum of 24 hours depends on your input arguments. In the output from a study that I have here I need 19 columns.

> sleep duration = dur_nightsleep_min
> sedentary time = dur_TINday_mi
> LPA time = dur_TLIGday_min
> MPA time = dur_TMODday_min
> VPA time = dur_TVIGday_min
> Total wear time = dur_nightandday_min
> Non-wear time = nonwear_hours
>
> One thing I am particular unsure is where the time of "nightwak_MOD/VIG/LIG" should be categorised as: sleep time or time spent on each intensity levels? If these are added to dur_nightsleep_min I assume it will be their duration spent in bed i.e. Time in Bed (onset minus offset of sleep)?

Response: You can consider them wakefulness during the night. The reason I labelled them as MOD/VIG/LIG is because I wanted to facilitate research on intensities in wakefullness. If that is not of interest to you then just collapse them as one wakefullness category.

> Thank you and best regards,

messages.body_plain:
Dear Vincent and Christopher,

thank you for this useful discussion that has really helped me to figure out how to do the same that Christopher is seeking to do: get activity classification as a function of time. (And, thank you, Vincent, for creating the GGIR analysis in the first place!)

To make sure I'm doing things correctly, I compared the daily activity derived from the files in the ms5.outraw folder to those in the "part5_daysummary_WW_L30M100.6V428.8_T5A5.csv" file in the Results folder and noticed that there are some differences. Generally, there are some more sedentary time and less time in LPA and MVPA when derived from the csv files in the ms5.outraw folder compared to the results file. The differences are sometimes only a couple of minutes but can be up to 20-30 min/day. Usually the differences add up to zero, so the duration of the day is the same. Would you have any idea where these differences come from?

Below I try to explain how I made the comparison, maybe there's something that I'm not doing correctly:

In part 5, I'm only using one bout duration to make things simpler:
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 5:
             # Key functions: Merging physical activity with sleep analyses
             #-------------------------------
             threshold.lig = c(30), threshold.mod = c(100.6),  threshold.vig = c(428.8),
             boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in <http://boutcriter.in> = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
             boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in <http://boutdur.in> = c(1), boutdur.lig = c(1),
             boutdur.mvpa = c(1),   timewindow = c("WW"),

This gives me class_id between 0-12 which I assume mean:

0 = Sleep period time + sleep

1 = Sleep period time + wakefulness (minimal movement)

2 = Sleep period time + wakefulness + light activity

3 = Sleep period time + wakefulness + moderate activity

4 = Sleep period time + wakefulness + vigorous activity

5 = Daytime + sustained inactivity

6 = Daytime + other inactivity

7 = Daytime + light activity

8 = Daytime + moderate activity

9 = Daytime + vigorous activity

10 = Daytime + MVPA bout, 1 min length

11 = Daytime + Inactivity bout, 1 min length

12 = Daytime + Light activity bout, 1 min length

To compare sedentary time, I compare (5+6+11)/12 (to change 5s epochs into 1 minute time) to dur_TINday_min in the results file.

LPA: (7+12)/12 to dur_TLIGday_min in the results file.

MVPA: (8+9+10)/12 to dur_TMODday_min+dur_TVIGday_min in the results file

Duration of the day: minutes in SED + LPA + MVPA compared to dur_day_min in results (these are usually the same, which I guess means that I'm defining the days correctly)

Best regards and thank you again!

Anna

messages.body_plain:
Hi Mark,

Good idea to make GGIR also applicable to Shimmer data.

Q1: For Actigraph, only start time, start date, sampling rate, and timestamp format specification from the first line are needed. However, if your data format is constant regarding timezone/country then this procedure could be simplified.
Q2: No problem, this is possible. There is variation between accelerometer brands anyway, so it is easier to add a few lines of code that look for column headers then to try to make all accelerometer brands adhere to one specific format.

In this <https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/tree/ax3csv> branch and more specifically this commit <https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/commit/86541f734eb03e52305e228cb5707e125cec4e90> I recently implemented similar functionality for Axivity AX3 csv-files. This might provide some inspiration. Note that this specific data format requires resampling of the data, which presumably is not needed for your data.

In this <https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues/87> issue Tuomo recommended that a more formal procedure for adding data formats to GGIR would be helpful. I agree, but I have not found the time for that yet (needless to say that I welcome others to work on this).

As I receive multiple help requests per week I have the following approach to helping:
- Once every couple of weeks I try to give quick answers to the questions related to GGIR that have accumulated in the google group and on GitHub.
- For more time consuming  issues or questions unrelated to GGIR I ask people to pay for my time (see also this <https://www.movementdata.nl/how-to-help-sustain-ggir> blog post where I motivate this). For example, the AX3-csv-file reading functionality I mentioned above was made possible thanks to financial compensation by the researcher.
- When it is obvious that an external person does all the work and my role is relatively minor then I do my part for free, or at least I try to if I have the time for it.

Let me know how you want to move forward.

Best regards,
Vincent

Hi Tom,
You should also include "dur_nightwak_and_IN45_min" because that is also wakefulness during the night, but simply with very little body movement.
Further, when you compare variables to check whether the calculations are correct, it is better to compare them at night or day level rather than at the person/file levels, because that is also how they are calculated.
The person level estimates are averages of the estimates across the days and only calculated at the very end. The additive logic at the day level is then slightly lost because of rounding. Also, the order of rounding and adding/subtracting might have an influence, especially when variables are calculated in log space like the intensity gradient variables in part2.

> Dear Vincent and group members!
>

> Within our validation study, we are analyzing geneactiv data. I have a few questions:
>
> 1. We wonder how the non-wear time (valid hours) of part2 and part5 can be different? (only slightly in the sum, but would be great to know).

Response:
Are you comparing the daily values or the total measurement values?
Can you post the exact variable names you are looking at? This is difficult for me to respond to.
What is the magnitude of the difference you found?
Are you looking at part5 MM output? I am asking because WW output would not be informative as it defines a daywindow differently.

> 2. It would be nice for our validation to get sedentary time out of the acc data. I know from a 2016 topic, that this feature was not available in GGIR back then. - Is it possible to get any sedentary time (or even a variable for it) now? Maybe trough calculations with other variables?
>

Response:
Inactivity is the term I used in GGIR to denote all time periods where people have little movement. I intentionally did not call it sedentary behaviour, because sedentary behavior implies that the activity type sitting can  be detected. As far as I know most accelerometer attachment locations (except thigh) are not able to provide reliable information on sitting type. The studies that claim to provide sitting time from a wrist or hip worn accelerometer usually come with low accuracy. Sitting time and inactivity time are always correlated, so it is not surprising that those studies find 70% accuracy (this simply comes from the fact that both co-occur), but real evidence that the activity type sitting can be distinguish from the activity type standing is often missing. By sticking to the more broader concept of "inactivity" I try to call the variable for what it represents. Some researchers like to interpret the inactivity estimates as sedentary behavior, I think it is confusing.

> 3. The visual reports and part5 output show a premature start of the acc measurment (about 1 hour) and also a premature ending of the measurment (again about 1 hour). We guess timeshift is the reason for that. Now we would like to know, if this "problem" is based on the acc itself (normally not, due to start time programmed MESZ +/- 0; Amsterdam) or from the GGIR analysis (MESZ -1; London )? This is not a big thing at all, but it would be nice to know if there is any easy way to change that for future analysis? (to change tz to amsterdam in chartime2iso8601, if "london" is default?)
>

Response:
Do you provide argument desiredtz to you call of g.shell.GGIR? This should handle the timezone.

messages.subject: GGIR version 1.7-1 & Contribution opportunities
messages.subject_clean: GGIR version 1.7-1 & Contribution opportunities
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

GGIR version 1.7-1 is now online, and you will find a summary of the main changes in the package's NEWS <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/news.html> page.

Most of these upgrades were made possible thanks to in-kind and financial contributions by GGIR users. Without these ongoing contributions, GGIR would simply not be sustainable. So, if you like GGIR and want it to be sustained and improved then get into action:

- Get involved in developing and testing the software code yourself, The more people involved in any open source software the better and more sustainable it gets. If you lack the skills then explore whether you can find funding to pay for a research software engineer in your department to dedicate a part of their time to GGIR.
- Consider the annual maintenance and support service <https://www.movementdata.nl/how-to-help-sustain-ggir> I provide, by which you support me to invest time to coordinate all this. Further, you can also use this service to get me to focus on issues that are of direct concern to you. Also, I am happy to discuss opportunities for giving a workshop/tutorial in your group - possibly in collaboration with your local physical activity/sleep expert.

Do not hesitate to get in touch if you have questions about how you can contribute.

Best regards,

Vincent
